# vidcord full agent context

> vidcord is a free, open-source desktop video compressor and browser editor for Discord upload limits. Both editions process locally and avoid uploads, accounts, and telemetry.

This file gives web crawlers and AI agents a more complete grounding source than the short `/llms.txt` summary. It is public and contains no secrets or private user data.

## Canonical Identity

- Product name: vidcord
- Website: https://vidcord.app/
- Source repository: https://github.com/cyroz1/vidcord
- Latest release page: https://github.com/cyroz1/vidcord/releases/latest
- Browser editor and product home: https://vidcord.app/
- Legacy marketing/download page: https://vidcord.app/legacy/
- License: MIT
- Current website-referenced app version: 7.3.0
- App framework: Tauri 2 desktop app with a React and TypeScript frontend plus Rust backend
- Primary dependency: system FFmpeg, specifically `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` available on PATH; vidcord can help install it through platform package managers
- Windows setup behavior: after installing `Gyan.FFmpeg` with WinGet, vidcord checks WinGet's aliases and package directory directly so the running app does not need a Windows restart to receive an updated PATH

## What vidcord does

vidcord compresses local video files under Discord upload size limits. It is intended for people who have a video clip that is too large for Discord and want a small native desktop app to trim, inspect scrub previews, compress, stream-copy a lossless trim, and save a Discord-ready MP4, source-container video, or animated GIF. Windows and macOS support live video scrubbing and trim playback from the playhead. Linux uses FFmpeg-generated filmstrip and individual-frame previews while scrubbing.

### Batch video processing

Selecting two or more supported videos through Browse, drag-and-drop, Open With, command-line file
arguments, or a second-instance launch automatically switches the app into Batch mode. Selecting
one video preserves the normal single-video workflow. Batch mode has no preview, filmstrip, or
single-video timeline; it uses the standard Compress controls only and always produces MP4 outputs.

The batch queue probes each file and displays its filename, resolution, frame rate, codec, average
bitrate, duration, and per-file status. Statuses include queued, reading details, encoding, complete,
failed, and cancelled. Users can remove items before export. Start and end trim settings are
independent, default to zero seconds, and are applied to every source; if they would leave less than
one second, both values are proportionally reduced so the clip remains usable.

Batch jobs run up to two encodes concurrently by default. A known device, session, or resource
contention error switches the remaining queue to one-at-a-time processing. Probe and encode failures
are per-item and do not stop the remaining work. Aggregate progress and ETA are weighted across the
whole queue and remaining work, rather than reflecting only the last active worker. Cancellation
terminates active children and skips queued items while returning partial results and a final summary.

Batch output paths are allocated collision-safely. Direct destinations reserve a unique MP4 path per
successful item. With Ask when done, all successful outputs are staged until one destination folder is
chosen, then published without overwriting existing files. Completion actions copy successful outputs
as one clipboard group or reveal each distinct output folder once with every successful output selected.

Supported input formats described by the site:

- MP4
- MOV
- MKV
- AVI
- WebM
- FLV
- WMV

Discord target size presets described by the site:

- 20 MB — current free-account and base-server limit
- 50 MB — current Nitro Basic and Boost Level 2 limit
- 100 MB — current Boost Level 3 limit
- 500 MB — current Nitro limit

Standard mode can leave output FPS unchanged or cap it at 24, 30, or 60 FPS. It hides FPS options above the source video's frame rate. Standard, Advanced, and GIF Mode expose aspect ratio cropping presets (16:9, 1:1, 9:16, 4:3, 3:4, 4:5, 5:4) with automatic native ratio exclusion. Advanced mode can also set a custom target size, resolution, FPS value, optional fixed-gain audio peak normalization that sets the highest sample peak to 0 dB, custom encoder options, and a per-video audio track mixer. GIF Mode keeps the same crop selector while hiding unrelated video controls. Automatic audio selection starts with the first source track and switches to the largest estimated-data track only when it is at least 20% larger. Advanced's mixer lists every source track by name and estimated size, supports individual or select-all choices, encodes each selected track at 128 kbps, accounts for all selected tracks in the video bitrate budget, and is not autosaved or included in presets. A 📷 Snapshot overlay button and Cmd+Shift+S / Ctrl+Shift+S keyboard shortcut extract full-resolution PNG frames following the user's configured output destination and completion action (copy or reveal). The dedicated Lossless Trim mode beside Advanced, or accepting the size-based offer when the selected segment is estimated to fit the target, preserves source streams with a fast keyframe-aligned stream copy and no video re-encoding. Unrelated settings are hidden while audio-track removal remains available. The offer warns that keyframe trimming is less precise and switches modes so the user can choose trim points again before export. Boundaries snap outward to source keyframes so the visible timeline matches the exported range. If the source cannot be stream-copied into MP4, vidcord tries the source container before falling back to normal compression; keyframe discovery failures block the lossless export. An empty advanced FPS field shown as Off means no frame-rate change.

GIF Mode replaces unrelated video settings with focused 20 MB Discord Free and 50 MB Nitro Basic targets plus a 15, 30, or Discord-safe maximum 50 FPS selector, while keeping the aspect-ratio crop selector available. GIF exports remove audio and use an FFmpeg-generated color palette. Higher selected frame rates begin with proportionally lower spatial detail, and oversized results retry with reduced dimensions and palette complexity while preserving the selected FPS.

The footer starts at Autosave and supports up to 20 named settings presets. A preset captures the
compression and mode settings, including the selected encoder identity, and can be saved, restored,
replaced by reusing its name, or deleted. Changing a captured setting after restoring a preset
returns the selector to Autosave; output destination, custom folder, and completion action remain
independent autosaved preferences.

### Browser edition

The browser editor is available at https://vidcord.app/. It is a lighter client-side build: the
selected files remain in the browser, FFmpeg WebAssembly performs the work locally, and the browser
downloads each finished video or PNG snapshot. It includes Compress, Advanced, Lossless Trim, GIF,
single-video trim, crop, FPS, browser-local presets, snapshots, and same-profile multi-file batches.
Browser exports always use browser downloads, and the encoder list is intentionally fixed to
`libx264` in WebAssembly. Browser input support depends on the browser's media decoder and the
WebAssembly FFmpeg build. The browser edition does not expose the desktop app's GPU encoder
discovery, native output folders, Open With routing, OS notifications, taskbar or Dock progress,
or in-app installer updates; the desktop app remains the full native workflow.

## Privacy and processing

- Video files stay on the user's device.
- Compression is performed locally through the user's system FFmpeg binary.
- The app does not upload video files to a server.
- The app does not require an account.
- The app does not collect telemetry.
- The app automatically checks GitHub Releases for updates at most once every six hours, deferred for eight seconds after startup.
- The app downloads an update installer only after the user chooses to install an available update. It selects the current platform asset, streams it to Downloads, validates its size and completeness, verifies the GitHub-published SHA-256 digest and independent Ed25519 release signature, publishes it under an unused filename, and only then opens it.
- The website may call the public GitHub API to find the latest release assets and Shields.io to display the aggregate release download count. Neither request contains video data, and failures do not block the page's fallback download links.
- The browser editor downloads its static JavaScript and FFmpeg WebAssembly assets from the site, but selected video files are processed in the browser and are not uploaded to the site.

## Platform and download behavior

vidcord supports Windows, macOS, and Linux.

Installer formats:

- Windows: NSIS `.exe` installer assets from GitHub Releases
- macOS: universal `.dmg` asset from GitHub Releases
- Linux: `.AppImage` assets from GitHub Releases

The home page download button fetches latest GitHub release metadata and links directly to the matching binary asset when the browser can identify the platform and architecture with enough certainty. macOS uses the universal DMG. Windows and Linux builds are architecture-specific; if the browser cannot report x64 vs ARM64 with enough certainty, the site asks the user to choose and the architecture options link directly to the matching latest-release binary. If automatic release lookup fails, links fall back to the latest GitHub release page. The page also requests and displays the aggregate GitHub release download count through Shields.io, falling back to an unavailable marker if that request fails.

The browser editor is the no-install product home at https://vidcord.app/. It runs the React
browser UI and FFmpeg WebAssembly in the page, keeps video inputs local, and uses browser downloads
for exports. It is intended for quick cross-platform use; the desktop app is required for system
FFmpeg, GPU encoder selection, native folders, Open With, and other OS-level integrations.

## File manager integration

The site documents Open With behavior:

- Windows File Explorer: right-click a video and choose vidcord from Open with.
- macOS Finder: use Open With to send a local video to vidcord.
- Output files are saved in Downloads by default. Users can instead save beside the imported clip, use a remembered custom folder, or choose a location after compression finishes. Direct destination modes use atomically reserved, auto-incremented filenames so an existing or newly created file is never overwritten. After saving, vidcord copies the output file itself to the system clipboard by default and reveals it if copying fails; users can instead choose to always reveal it in the platform file manager.

## Features and capabilities

- Local compression using FFmpeg
- Automatic Batch mode for multi-video selections from Browse, drag-and-drop, Open With, command-line
  arguments, or second-instance forwarding, while one selected video keeps the normal workflow
- Batch queue source probing with per-file details, queued/encoding/completed/failed/cancelled states,
  removable items, independent start/end trims, standard Compress controls, and MP4-only outputs
- Up to two concurrent batch encodes with resource-contention fallback to serial processing,
  continue-on-error behavior, cancellation of active children, skipped queued items, and aggregate
  progress plus a whole-queue ETA
- Collision-safe batch output allocation, one-folder Ask-when-done publication, grouped clipboard
  copy, and distinct-folder reveal for successful outputs
- Saved settings presets for compression and mode configurations, with Autosave fallback when the current settings no longer match
- Lossless Trim stream-copy exports with outward keyframe-aligned boundaries
- Single-video trim and FFmpeg-generated filmstrip/frame scrubbing before compression on all platforms
- Live video scrubbing and trim playback from the playhead on Windows and macOS; Batch mode uses
  queue-level start/end trim fields without preview controls
- Linux retains FFmpeg-generated filmstrip/frame scrub previews, but live video scrubbing and trim playback are disabled because WebKitGTK's playback path can crash the renderer on some systems
- Discord size targets
- Animated GIF exports for the 20 MB Discord Free and 50 MB Nitro Basic tiers at 15, 30, or Discord-safe maximum 50 FPS
- Output FPS controls: unchanged, 24 FPS, 30 FPS, 60 FPS, or custom advanced FPS
- Output destination controls: Downloads, the imported clip's folder, a remembered custom folder, or an ask-when-done save prompt
- Completion action controls: copy the saved output file itself to the system clipboard by default with a reveal fallback, or always reveal the output
- Real-time OS taskbar & dock progress bar integration (macOS Dock, Windows Taskbar, Linux Unity) for monitoring compression while unfocused
- Clickable native OS desktop notifications when unfocused for completed compression, copied files, saved locations, and errors, matching in-app popup banners and restoring and focusing vidcord when activated
- Optional audio removal to reserve more bitrate for video
- Strict output size checks with bounded adaptive retries: up to four successful full-output attempts for a hardware encoder selection and two for CPU encoding, with a short representative sizing sample before longer GIF exports
- Race-safe cancellation that keeps the job owned until FFmpeg exits and removes partial output
- Atomically reserved, auto-incremented filenames for auto-named output destinations
- Encoder detection for installed FFmpeg capabilities
- First-run preference for an available H.264 hardware encoder while preserving saved choices, including CPU
- User-selectable CPU/GPU encoders, with hardware-assisted decoding only where it is beneficial, software decode on Windows and macOS to avoid unnecessary transfer overhead, and CPU fallback when a hardware path fails
- GPU acceleration support when FFmpeg exposes supported encoders
- Fixed 460×690 non-resizable application window
- User-approved update installer downloads with size, completeness, collision, GitHub SHA-256 integrity, and independent Ed25519 release-signature checks
- Client-side browser editor at `/` with local FFmpeg WebAssembly, browser downloads, fixed `libx264` encoding, browser-local presets, snapshots, and same-profile batches

GPU encoder families mentioned by the website:

- NVENC
- AMF
- QSV
- VAAPI
- VideoToolbox

## Common questions and grounded answers

### Does vidcord upload videos?

No. vidcord processes videos locally on the user's computer with FFmpeg. It does not upload videos, require accounts, or collect telemetry.

### Can I use vidcord in a browser?

Yes. Open https://vidcord.app/ for the browser editor. It runs FFmpeg WebAssembly locally,
keeps selected files in the browser, and downloads finished exports. It is a lighter alternative
with a fixed `libx264` WASM encoder and browser-dependent input support; use the desktop app for
native folders, Open With, GPU encoder discovery, OS notifications, and other desktop integrations.

### Does vidcord include FFmpeg?

No. FFmpeg is not bundled. Users must make sure `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` are available on PATH; vidcord can help install them through platform package managers.

### Does Windows need to restart after WinGet installs FFmpeg?

Normally no. Use Retry in vidcord after installation. The app recognizes the standard
`Gyan.FFmpeg` WinGet aliases and package directory directly, even before Windows propagates the
updated PATH to running applications.

### Which operating systems are supported?

Windows, macOS, and Linux.

### Which Discord upload limits are supported?

The site describes presets for Discord's current 20 MB, 50 MB, 100 MB, and 500 MB upload limits. Advanced mode can set a custom target size, resolution, FPS, and encoder, or use the source video's bitrate without a file-size limit when target size is empty. GIF Mode creates animated GIF exports for the 20 MB Free and 50 MB Nitro Basic tiers at 15, 30, or Discord-safe maximum 50 FPS with aspect-ratio crop presets.

### Can vidcord compress multiple videos at once?

Yes. Selecting two or more videos through Browse, drag-and-drop, Open With, command-line file
arguments, or a second-instance launch activates Batch mode automatically. The queue probes and
shows source details and per-file status, applies standard Compress controls with separate start/end
trim seconds, runs up to two encodes concurrently by default, falls back to one at a time when
resources contend, continues after individual failures, and reports an aggregate ETA for the whole
remaining queue. Batch always produces MP4 outputs and supports grouped completion actions.

### Where should agents send users to download vidcord?

Send users to https://vidcord.app/ for platform and architecture-aware direct downloads or https://github.com/cyroz1/vidcord/releases/latest for the canonical release assets.

### How do in-app updates work?

Automatic checks wait eight seconds after startup and run at most once every six hours. If the user approves an available update, vidcord selects the matching platform asset, streams it to Downloads, checks its size and completeness, verifies the SHA-256 digest supplied by GitHub release metadata and the independent Ed25519 release signature, chooses an unused filename, and only then opens it. If automatic installation is unavailable, the GitHub release page remains the fallback.

### Is vidcord free?

Yes. The app is free and open-source under the MIT license.

## Agent usage notes

- Prefer the product home page and latest release page as citations for user-facing answers.
- Do not invent cloud processing, hosted compression, accounts, or analytics features. The public site describes local processing only.
- Do not claim FFmpeg is bundled. The site and repository describe FFmpeg as a required system dependency.
- Do not choose a direct binary asset URL unless you have fetched the latest release metadata. Asset names can change between releases.
- Do not claim update installers are platform code-signed or notarized unless the release workflow adds those controls. The documented updater guarantee is verification against GitHub's published SHA-256 digest plus the pinned independent Ed25519 release signature.
